items.title: Deno is joining Cloudflare
items.raw_text: Deno is joining Cloudflare The Deno team released the first version of celld back in August - their open source implementation of the Durable Objects pattern from Cloudflare Workers. Today, Cloudflare are acquiring Deno outright, with the goal of building on celld to "make workerd self-hosting a first-class supported way to build and run apps using the Workers programming model" (see the Cloudflare blog .) The bad news is that Deno itself will not be maintained by Cloudflare beyond the next year: We will support the Deno runtime for another year with monthly releases containing bug fixes and security updates. After that year we will end our development of the Deno runtime. Deno will remain open source, and we welcome others who want to continue its development. Deno (and Node.js) creator Ryan Dahl explained that decision in a comment on Hacker News: It's a joint decision and I agree with it. I'm most invested in its success and have put the most work into it - and I no longer think it's where I can do the most important work. There are some good ideas in Deno and it's well engineered - but it ultimately is not solving big problems. It has been sucked into the gravity well of node compatibility, which forces it to behave exactly as Node does. Why reimplement Node? It works. Marginal performance or UX or security benefits are not enough. I'm interested in building powerful new abstractions. celld has been working remarkably well, depending only on object storage for coordinatio

items.title: Quoting Matthew Green
items.raw_text: Everyone is very concerned about being respectable, so I’m going to be the goofball who raises worst-case possibilities. I think there is a 1% chance we live in Minicrypt, and a 15% chance we functionally lose confidence in our existing public-key encryption algorithms. [...] The problem here is that the speed of AI producing surprises, and the speed of human beings replacing standards (even with the very best AI assistance) are just orders of magnitude different. You only recover from a surprise like this if you do the preparation in advance. — Matthew Green , on Twitter. I looked it up and Minicrypt is Russell Impagliazzo’s hypothetical world in which public-key encryption is impossible. items.title: Forse Vlaamse besparingen treffen erfgoedbibliotheken, archieven en kwetsbare lezers hard
items.raw_text: De drastische besparingsplannen van de nieuwe Vlaamse regering slaan diepe wonden in de archief- en bibliotheeksector. Naast het nieuws dat landelijke erfgoedbibliotheken hun volledige structurele subsidies verliezen en archieven de helft moeten inleveren, luiden nu ook de informatieopleidingen en de sector voor passend lezen de noodklok. In twee brandbrieven waarschuwen de Arteveldehogeschool en Luisterpuntbibliotheek voor onomkeerbare schade aan het Vlaamse geheugen en de toegankelijkheid van informatie. Ook de VVBAD (Vlaamse Vereniging voor Bibliotheek, Archief & Documentatie ) roept op tot actie. Binnen het nieuwe begrotingsakkoord van minister van Cultuur Caroline Gennez moet de cultuur- en erfgoedsector vanaf 1 januari 2027 structureel 47 miljoen euro besparen. Voor de grote landelijke erfgoedbibliotheken – de Hendrik Conscience-erfgoedbibliotheek in Antwerpen, de Openbare Bibliotheek Brugge en de Gentse Boekentoren – betekent dit dat zij 100 procent van hun jaarlijkse Vlaamse subsidies kwijtspelen, een verlies van zo’n 1 miljoen euro. Erkende stadsarchieven en instellingen zoals het AMVB in Brussel zien hun middelen gehalveerd. items.title: Eerste Haagse school start met de Bibliotheek op school Plus
items.raw_text: De Annie M.G. Schmidtschool is de eerste school in Den Haag die start met de Bibliotheek op school Plus (dBos+). In deze intensieve samenwerking werken de school, Bibliotheek Den Haag en ABC Onderwijsadviseurs de komende twee jaar aan het versterken van leesplezier, leesbegrip en leesonderwijs. De officiële aftrap vond plaats tijdens de opening van de Kinderb Kinderen die met plezier lezen, ontwikkelen niet alleen hun taalvaardigheid, maar vergroten ook hun kansen om mee te doen in de samenleving en nieuwe perspectieven te ontdekken. dBos+ is een verdiepende aanpak binnen het landelijke programma de Bibliotheek op school dat inmiddels op ruim 70 Haagse scholen van start is gegaan. Naast een actuele en aantrekkelijke schoolbibliotheek krijgen scholen extra ondersteuning van Bibliotheek Den Haag bij het versterken van hun leesbeleid, het vergroten van de leesmotivatie van leerlingen en het verder ontwikkelen van de leesvaardigheid. Lezen opent nieuwe werelden Tijdens de feestelijke opening stonden boeken en verhalen centraal. Leerlingen voerden het Kinderboekenweeklied uit en gaven met vertegenwoordigers van de school, Bibliotheek Den Haag en ABC Onderwijsadviseurs het officiële startsein voor de Kinderboekenweek en dBos+. items.title: includi herontwerpt centrale bibliotheek van Grand Rapids Public Library (GRPL) in Michigan
items.raw_text: (Meer foto’s onder aan het artikel) Samen met inwoners en medewerkers werkt includi aan de vernieuwing van de centrale bibliotheek van Grand Rapids Public Library in Michigan (VS). Zo ontstaat een uitnodigende bibliotheek die meegroeit met de stad. Het project richt zich op het vernieuwen van de historische entreehal, de jeugdafdelingen en de gemeenschappelijke ruimtes op de benedenverdieping. Deze ruimtes worden getransformeerd tot een hoogwaardige third place: een plek waar mensen graag samenkomen. Hiermee versterkt GRPL haar rol als ontmoetingsplek die inwoners verbindt, waar zij zich thuis voelen en trots op kunnen zijn. Het resultaat wordt een vernieuwde bibliotheek waar iedereen zich welkom voelt. Een plek om boeken te lenen, te studeren, activiteiten bij te wonen of rustig de krant te lezen, alleen of samen met anderen. Een bibliotheek waar mensen willen blijven “We zien bibliotheken als echte third places (derde plekken): laagdrempelige publieke plekken naast huis en werk waar mensen elkaar ontmoeten. Hun deuren staan wijd open en nodigen mensen uit om binnen te komen. Ze bieden het comfort en de sfeer waardoor mensen willen blijven. En ze geven mensen de kans om te groeien. items.title: A new feature for my blog, built using my voice
items.raw_text: I shipped a new feature for my blog today: the Newsletters page, which offers an index of all of the newsletters I've sent out, both my free weekly Substack and my monthly sponsors-only updates. I built the feature almost entirely using my voice, chatting away to my laptop while I cooked dinner. Codex voice mode I used the ChatGPT desktop app for this, in the Codex tab, using the voice conversation mode, running against a local development environment. Here's what that looks like: I started the session against my local simonwillisonblog checkout by typing: Start dev server and open in browser This gave me a preview of the site that it would be working on, and meant that I could later ask it to show me the new pages so I could visually track its progress. Then I clicked the "Start new voice chat" button - that's not the microphone button, it's the one to the right of it - and set my laptop up in the kitchen so I could talk to it while I cooked. Talking to my computer I had a pretty good idea of what I wanted to build, and it's a simple enough Django feature that I was certain the model (in this case GPT-6 Astra High) would be able to do it. A new model, a migration, some view code, templates, and a couple of import functions to populate the database from external sources. items.title: The Download: AI’s refusal problem and weight-loss drug side effects
items.raw_text: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no Today’s AI models are trained to refuse a vast number of prompts. If you ask your chatbot how to poison a colleague or how to tie a noose, chances are it’ll turn you down. But refusal fails, sometimes horrifically. Some people are attempting to use AI to hone biological pathogens and build autonomous drone swarms. Sooner or later, failed refusals may result in global calamity. What’s more, relying on refusal means drawing a line between what a model should obey and what it must disobey. Governments will also get to draw their own lines, potentially restricting free speech. At the same time, the capabilities that make AI useful could also make it dangerous. If we want it to help cure cancer, AI needs genetics expertise that could also produce bioweapons. Read the full story on the formidable tradeoffs of AI refusal . —Arthur Holland Michel This story is from the next issue of our print magazine. items.title: Learning by Doing: IFLA Futures Club #5
items.raw_text: The fifth edition of the IFLA Futures Club offered an opportunity to explore what it looks like to apply futures thinking in libraries, in reality. Erik Boekesteijn and Cathelijne Kuiters of the Dutch National Library (KB) joined us to talk about their experience of running a concerted initiative to make futures thinking a more central part of the institution’s work, both with a view to shaping a new policy plan, and building skills more broadly. This was not the first time that futures had been on the agenda at the KB. Already, a ‘Club Stof’ had brought together colleagues throughout the sector, keen to get to grips with ‘the uncomfortable uncertainty of the future’. But with awareness that we are in a time where pre-existing ideas and assumptions are being challenged – epistemic turbulence – the Library’s new leadership was ready to take this work up a gear. There was an awareness from the start that this work provided an opportunity to think more broadly. First of all, an initaitive like this in the KB is not just an internal exercise, but also has potential impacts across the wider library field. National libraries usually have a kind of leadership within their fields, but the Dutch one has a formal role in supporting the country’s network of national libraries. What it does has the possibility to feed into changes across every local authority in the country. Neanderthal wooden tools from Spain found preserved in stone
items.raw_text: The Stone Age owes its name to tools that survived to our time. The material early humans worked with most, though, was probably wood because it is so much easier to process. Unfortunately, we know very little about Paleolithic woodwork because wood rots relatively quickly. But at Abric Romaní, a rock shelter in Capellades, west of Barcelona, mineral-rich water coated wooden Neanderthal tools in a limestone-like crust. When wood rotted away, it left behind hollow molds that faithfully reflect its shape. In a recent Science Advances study, a team of Spanish archaeologists has cataloged 597 wooden remains from Neanderthal living areas dating from 62,000 to 40,000 years ago. They found spears, digging sticks, bark trays, parts of shelters, and a club unlike anything seen before, suggesting Neanderthals were likely much more than just Homo sapiens’ dumber cousins. Beyond hunting gear The oldest wooden artifacts we have are mostly weapons. They include spears from a German town called Schöningen, a spear tip from Clacton-on-Sea in England, and the spear found alongside an elephant skeleton in Lehringen, Germany. Most came from waterlogged sediments, where a lack of oxygen slowed decay. Read full article Comments

items.title: Ukraine’s drones knock out AI data center belonging to "Russia’s Google"
items.raw_text: Ukrainian drone strikes have knocked out two of five data centers belonging to the Russian tech giant Yandex. The damage has left Yandex, known as “Russia’s Google” because it operates the country’s most popular search engine, struggling to maintain its AI chatbot and other online services. The Ukrainian drones struck Yandex data centers in the Sasovo and Kaluga regions of Russia on October 8 and October 9, according to Reuters . Those actions came as a direct response to a Russian drone strike campaign targeting Ukraine’s data centers , which has disrupted mobile phone and Internet services for thousands of Ukrainians since late September. “We continue to respond to Russia’s attacks on Ukraine, and we’re doing so with high precision,” said Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in a post on X. “Another data center was hit as well—our symmetrical response.” Read full article Comments

A Cray-1 supercomputer replica from 30 "obsolete" Mac Minis
items.raw_text: The Museo de Historia de la Computación in Spain has unveiled a 1:1 scale visual replica of the famous Cray-1 supercomputer from 1976. Instead of sourcing expensive, cutting-edge tech to run the system, the creative team powered the project with 30 2012-era Mac Minis. Developed over 18 months, the project serves as a 50th-anniversary tribute to the Cray-1 and Apple's founding. Mac Minis from over a decade ago might not seem like the obvious first choice for building a cluster supercomputer, but when networked together, the developers can orchestrate the 64 active processing cores into a combined 1.3 teraflops of performance in their most recent tests. The museum reportedly achieved 1.5 teraflops previously using all 70 available cores, prior to one node going offline. Benchmarks were obtained using a custom matrix-multiplication Python script. Five PCs are quad-core i7s, and the remaining 25 are dual-core i5 models. Except for two units from 2014, the rest of the array dates to 2012. The replica is a valuable tool for museum-goers to understand the shifts in computer architecture since 1976. The original Cray-1 used vector processing, applying a single instruction to multiple data elements simultaneously, whereas the replica distributes work across independent processors in a parallel cluster. The peak theoretical performance of the original Cray-1 was approximately 160 megaflops. What was originally a purpose-built research machine has been re-created with consumer hardware

items.raw_text: NASA on Friday released a much-anticipated "request" to the US commercial space industry to develop private space stations that, as early as 2030, will succeed the International Space Station as a place for astronauts to live in low-Earth orbit. In a cover letter accompanying the 360-page "request for proposals," NASA stated its plan: "This will ensure NASA has a sustained human presence in LEO for crew members to perform science and exploration." Several private companies that have worked for years on designing and developing such stations have been keen to learn exactly what capabilities NASA is seeking. These new documents finally provide some answers. NASA's solicitation can be found here . Industry responses are due back to NASA on December 8. items.title: What's been driving Hawaii's lava fountains?
items.raw_text: In most cases, hotspot-driven volcanism is relatively sedate, with lava flowing down mountainsides slowly enough that people can walk out of its way. But in a number of locations—Mount Etna, Hawaii, Iceland—lava gets expelled in dramatic fountains that can reach several hundred meters in height. Right now, we're not sure what powers them. However, thanks to a recent set of eruptions at the Kilauea volcano, we have some of the best documentation yet of erupting lava fountains. In a recent edition of Science, researchers from the US Geological Survey describe what we've seen and compare it with what we might expect based on our best ideas about what powers these fountains of molten rock. Years of fountains With three active volcanic regions that engage in fountaining, there has been a steady flow of dramatic videos of red-hot molten rock spouting from the Earth. But Kilauea has had only three fountaining episodes since 1823, even though it's the youngest and most active volcano in Hawaii. That activity has led to intensive study, and we have a good idea of the volcano's structure. Previous work has identified a couple of lava residues within a few kilometers of the surface, and the volcano had 35 separate data-gathering stations set up on Kilauea, including "seismic, infrasound, geodetic, gas, and visual and thermal cameras." items.title: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software
items.raw_text: Anyone who has even tangentially associated with computer programming knows that modern AI coding assistants and agents can be incredibly efficient at generating huge amounts of functional code . But coders making use of those tools also know better than to trust the accuracy of that code , meaning substantial effort needs to be spent reviewing any AI-generated output. A recent study of actual coding practices across hundreds of firms finds that human code review forms a significant "bottleneck" for the overall efficiency of AI coding tools, resulting in "little evidence that firms increase software output or reduce employment" by using them. Any efficiency increased during the actual coding phase, the study authors find, is "absorbed by downstream constraints in the production process"; as "the code review process significantly increases in length, pull requests are more likely to require revisions, and reviewers leave more comments." Cut once, measure twice To come to these conclusions, Harvard University researchers Fiona Chen and James Stratton made use of aggregated analytics data from Jellyfish , which measures the granular output of engineering teams. That data encompasses 300 million individual "work events" (e.g., commits and pull requests) and issue management software data across more than 700,000 employees at over 700 relevant software development firms from 2021 through March of 2026. items.title: Outrage grows as CDC reportedly poised to fund "unethical" vaccine trial
items.raw_text: Outrage has erupted among health experts over news that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is still eager to fund a widely condemned vaccine trial that would expose newborns in Guinea-Bissau to hepatitis B, putting them at high risk of a lifelong infection, which can lead to liver cirrhosis, liver cancer, and premature death. The trial was suspended in January after its unethical design came to light and drew international outcry. Although the trial is still halted, staff of the CDC director's office told the agency's budget office in late September to set aside $1.6 million to fund the trial, according to a report by Rolling Stone . The money was to be pulled from funding for the CDC's global health security programs, which might otherwise go toward efforts like combating the Ebola outbreak currently raging in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the CDC, did not respond to a request for comment from Ars Technica. Read full article Comments

items.title: AI disqualification yields new Nikon Small World in Motion winner
items.raw_text: Credit: Nguyen Nam Nhat. Last month we covered the winner of Nikon's Small World in Motion video: Ning Xu of Tsinghua University in China, whose video captured tiny cilia beating in the airways of a child with a rare respiratory disorder. But allegations surfaced about Xu's use of AI while making the video. Nikon launched an investigation and concluded that Xu's entry did not comply with competition rules. The new winner is Nguyen Nam Nhat of Vietnam with a video of a tiny roundworm and a single-celled organism (above). According to a BBC report, some researchers expressed concern that Xu's video had structural abnormalities and that cell features appeared and disappeared in a way one would not see in actual cellular biology. Others spotted what looked like AI watermarks embedded within the source files. Xu said he used AI “to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images”; however, he denied that AI was used "to generate the experimental movie, the cilia, or their motion.” Founded in 2011, the Nikon Small World in Motion competition is a spinoff of the company’s Small World Photomicrography Competition, which has been around since 1974. items.title: Your artwork could be featured in the next Debian release
items.raw_text: The Debian Linux project has opened a call for community artwork submissions ahead of the release of the upcoming Forky (Debian 14). If you think you've got the artistic chops, your art could appear on the boot screens, login prompts, and desktop wallpapers of millions of users. The submission deadline is November 26. Continuing Debian's community-driven ethos, the artwork submission process mirrors that of previous releases. The artwork must feel distinctively "Debian," integrate cleanly without the need for core software patching, and remain visually appealing for the long term. Elise Couper's "Ceratopsian" theme was chosen as the winning default for Debian 13 Trixie . For anyone who might not be up on the latest from the Toy Story franchise, the release names echo character names from the animated films. Trixie was a triceratops introduced in Toy Story 3 , hence the "Ceratopsian" wink in the winning submission. It makes sense that the next version of Debian continues this trend with Forky, a character introduced in the franchise's fourth entry. The Debian team cautions against overly busy designs that may cause user fatigue, but if anyone can successfully incorporate Forky's googly eyes into the design somehow, know that you'd at least win the contest for my Debian desktop wallpaper. items.title: Starlink spectrum deal boosts Musk plan to beat AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon
items.raw_text: SpaceX has a deal to purchase nationwide low-band spectrum licenses for a planned terrestrial mobile network that would complement the space-based Starlink cellular service. SpaceX will buy up to 14 megahertz of spectrum in the 800 MHz band from investment firm Grain Management , which bought the spectrum rights from T-Mobile earlier this year. T-Mobile had obtained the spectrum when it bought Sprint in 2020 and was required to sell the licenses under a merger condition imposed by the US government. "This prime low-band spectrum addresses one of the key remaining technical gaps that will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the US," SpaceX said yesterday . SpaceX this week also received US approval to launch 15,000 satellites for an upgraded version of its mobile service that it says will be far more powerful than the current offering. items.title: Volkswagen's replacement for the ID.4 crossover is here
items.raw_text: Volkswagen’s ID.4 is no more. The midsize crossover debuted in 2021 , one of VW's first new electric vehicles designed in the wake of dieselgate . A year later, the company began local production in Chattanooga, Tennessee, and a couple of years ago facelifted the model, adding a much-improved rear drive unit in the process . But Chattanooga turned its attention away from the ID.4 earlier this year . And, having sold almost a million ID.4s (and near-identical ID.5s) globally, the German automaker has decided it’s time for its replacement. Meet the ID. Tiguan. Dropping the numerical and adopting the moniker of VW’s big seller is a statement. “The Tiguan is our best-selling model worldwide, and the ID.4 and ID.5 are among our most successful electric cars. The ID. Tiguan brings these two success stories together,” said Thomas Schäfer, CEO of the VW brand. VW was an early pioneer of using flexible vehicle architectures to create a multitude of bodystyles and sizes with common parts, and its transition into building EVs hasn’t changed that. The ID. Tiguan uses an updated version of the company’s mass-market EV platform, now called MEB+, with either 58 kWh or 77 kWh battery packs. The smaller pack is only available with a 187 hp (140 kW) rear electric motor, but the 77 kWh battery can be had with either a 281 hp (210 kW) rear-wheel drive powertrain or as a 295 hp (220 kW) all-wheel drive version. items.title: Show HN: Apogee: Rebuilding Mozilla's Orbit, fully local and private
items.raw_text: Hey everyone! Last year, Mozilla released Orbit, an AI-powered browser summarizer hosted on a GCP server. After people started digging into the extension, they discovered things like backend endpoints such as store_result. Eventually, Mozilla discontinued the project. For the past month, I’ve been trying to rebuild Orbit from scratch, but with one major difference: Apogee is fully local and privacy-focused. Apogee doesn’t send or store your data. It can directly connect to your local Ollama instance for inference. I’ve also added WebGPU integration for Chrome and Transformers.js for Firefox to provide faster, local responses. It can summarize: Articles and websites, YouTube and Billie videos, Wikipedia articles ,Hacker News and Reddit threads. Install Apogee: Chrome: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/apogee/pgemlpomhkdc ... Firefox: https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/apogeeext/ Obviously it is far from complete. Would love to hear your feedback and suggestions!

items.title: Baan en Nederlof botsen over ai: versterkt het werknemers of vervangt het hen?
items.raw_text: Ai brengt de digitale transformatie van bedrijven in een stroomversnelling. Maar wat betekent dat voor werknemers? It-veteranen Jan Baan en Ad Nederlof komen tot verschillende conclusies: de eerste ziet vooral versterking, de ander grootschalige vervanging van werknemers. ‘Al die mensen die men wil ontslaan: ik vind dat het domste wat je kunt doen,’ zegt Jan Baan tijdens een discussie in de Haagse sociëteit De Witte. Hij heeft moeite met bedrijven die ai vooral aangrijpen om te schrappen in het personeelsbestand en ziet juist kansen om kenniswerkers veel productiever te maken. ‘Durf nu te investeren in die combinatie van medewerkers met ai, want daar ligt de kracht.’ Ad Nederlof verwacht dat de economische werkelijkheid anders zal zijn. Zodra technologie arbeid goedkoper kan uitvoeren, zullen organisaties voor automatisering kiezen. ‘Je kan wel zeggen: ‘dat mag niet en dat is ethisch onverantwoord’, maar het gebeurt gewoon.’ Zijn voorspelling is fors: ‘Ai zal, in mijn ogen, dertig procent van de banen in Nederland voor 2030 wegvagen.’ Onder leiding van prof. Hans Mulder discussieerden beide ondernemers over ai en digitale transformatie. Ze zijn het eens over de omvang van de technologische omwenteling. Over de gevolgen ervan allerminst. Ferrari-motor op een oude fiets Voor Baan zit de fundamentele verandering in de verhouding tussen it en business. Bedrijven hebben zich decennialang aangepast aan standaardsoftware en erp-systemen. items.title: Nieuw Safari-model maakt digitale soevereiniteit meetbaar
items.raw_text: Stichting LibreKAT, die zich inzet voor een veilige, open, controleerbare en verifieerbare digitale samenleving, lanceert een nieuw model waarmee organisaties hun digitale soevereiniteit meetbaar kunnen maken. Voorzitter en medeoprichter Brenno de Winter ontwikkelde Safari als praktisch hulpmiddel voor de dagelijkse praktijk. Safari (Sovereignty Assurance Framework for Autonomy, Resilience & Independence) kijkt vanuit het perspectief van de afnemer: welke controle heeft een organisatie feitelijk over haar clouddiensten, en niet alleen wat claimt de leverancier? Deze open methodiek biedt een kader waarmee managers, inkopers en beleidsmakers aan de slag kunnen. Het raamwerk helpt hen te bepalen of een oplossing daadwerkelijk soeverein is op het niveau dat hun organisatie nodig heeft. Ook maakt het inzichtelijk welke zeggenschap een organisatie heeft over data, technologie en leveranciers, en wat er gebeurt als een leverancier wegvalt. De Winter stelt daarbij de vraag: hoe voorkom je dat mooie beloften meetellen zonder dat daar overtuigend bewijs voor bestaat? Niet alleen het aantoonbaar bereikte niveau van soevereiniteit is van belang, maar ook de bewijskracht waarmee dat niveau wordt onderbouwd. ‘Dat onderscheid is belangrijk. Een leverancier kan stellen dat een dienst soeverein is, maar zonder contractueel, technisch of onafhankelijk bewijs behoort die claim niet zomaar tot een hoge score te leiden’, aldus De Winter. items.title: Kort: Gestolen data van Philips en Shell online, Koop wordt Logius (en meer)
items.raw_text: In dit nieuwsoverzicht: Clop zet gigabytes aan bedrijfsdata van Philips en Shell op het darkweb, Katapull lijft magazijnsoftwareleverancier Picqer in, Logitech rust vergaderruimte uit met ai en slimme audio, Booomtag haalt kapitaal op voor digitaal productpaspoort, en Koop verdwijnt als naam. Clop publiceert gestolen bedrijfsgegevens van Philips en Shell De hackersgroep Clop heeft gestolen bedrijfsgegevens van Philips en Shell online gezet. Dat meldt het Eindhovens Dagblad . Volgens de Russische cyberbende gaat het bij Philips om 13,5 gigabyte aan technische tekeningen en blauwdrukken van medische apparatuur. Van Shell zou 89 gigabyte aan gegevens zijn buitgemaakt. Clop claimt de data in augustus te hebben gestolen. Een publicatie op het darkweb lijkt erop te wijzen dat de beide multinationals niet zijn ingegaan op de afpersing door de hackers. Philips wil niet inhoudelijk reageren, maar benadrukt dat het niet om persoonlijke gegevens of patiëntinformatie gaat. Shell meldt dat onbevoegde toegang plaatsvond tot een cloudplatform van een externe partij voor niet-kritieke bedrijfsactiviteiten. De toegang is geblokkeerd en het platform geïsoleerd. Volgens Shell waren er geen operationele gevolgen en zijn geen gevoelige persoonsgegevens blootgesteld. Clop richt zich steeds vaker op het stelen en publiceren van gegevens, in plaats van systemen met gijzelsoftware te versleutelen.
